reg_deadline.en: Registration for November 3 closed 30 days before the election, on October 4, 2026. Not sure you're registered? Check the Voter Information Center at vote.ri.gov.
reg_deadline.es: El registro para el 3 de noviembre cerró 30 días antes de la elección, el 4 de octubre de 2026. ¿No sabes si estás registrado? Revisa el Voter Information Center en vote.ri.gov.
reg_deadline.quote: Registration for any election shall close on the thirtieth (30th) day preceding an election

mail_request.en: Regular applications closed October 13, 2026. Can't vote in person? Apply for an emergency mail ballot at your local board of canvassers by 4 p.m. on Monday, November 2. It must reach the Board of Elections by 8 p.m. on Election Day.
mail_request.es: Las solicitudes regulares cerraron el 13 de octubre de 2026. ¿No puedes votar en persona? Solicita una boleta de emergencia por correo en la junta de escrutinio local (local board of canvassers) a más tardar a las 4 p. m. del lunes 2 de noviembre. Debe llegar a la Junta Electoral (Board of Elections) a más tardar a las 8 p. m. del Día de las Elecciones.
mail_request.quote: The emergency mail ballot application, when duly executed, shall be delivered in person or by mail so that it shall be received by the local board, or received electronically through the portal established by § 17-20-2.3, not later than four o’clock (4:00) p.m. on the last day preceding the date of the election.
mail_request.en_after: Mail ballot applications, including emergency ones, closed at 4 p.m. on November 2. Vote at your polling place on Election Day, 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.
mail_request.es_after: Las solicitudes de boleta por correo, incluidas las de emergencia, cerraron a las 4 p. m. del 2 de noviembre. Vota en tu lugar de votación el Día de las Elecciones, de 7 a. m. a 8 p. m.

mail_return.en: Your ballot must reach the Board of Elections by 8 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3. A postmark isn't enough. Mail it by Tuesday, October 27, use a drop box, or hand it in at the Board of Elections, 2000 Plainfield Pike, Suite A, Cranston.
mail_return.es: Tu boleta debe llegar a la Junta Electoral (Board of Elections) a más tardar a las 8 p. m. del martes 3 de noviembre. El matasellos no basta. Envíala a más tardar el martes 27 de octubre, déjala en un buzón de entrega o entrégala en la Junta Electoral, 2000 Plainfield Pike, Suite A, Cranston.
mail_return.quote: Allow at least seven (7) mailing days to ensure your mail ballot arrives by 8 p.m. on Election Day. ... Option 3: Hand deliver the sealed envelope to the Board of Elections: 2000 Plainfield Pike, Suite A Cranston, RI 02921 The Board of Elections must receive your mail ballot by 8 p.m. on Election Day
mail_return.en_after: Use a drop box, or hand it in at the Board of Elections, 2000 Plainfield Pike, Suite A, Cranston, by 8 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3. It has to be received by then, so the mail is too slow now. On Election Day, every polling place also has a box for sealed mail ballots.
mail_return.es_after: Usa un buzón de entrega o entrégala en la Junta Electoral (Board of Elections), 2000 Plainfield Pike, Suite A, Cranston, a más tardar a las 8 p. m. del martes 3 de noviembre. Tiene que llegar antes de esa hora, así que el correo ya es muy lento. El Día de las Elecciones, cada lugar de votación también tiene una caja para boletas por correo selladas.

early_hours.en: Early voting is at a location your city or town picks, during its regular business hours, and ends at 4 p.m. on Monday, November 2. Call your local board of canvassers for hours.
early_hours.es: La votación anticipada es en un lugar que elige tu ciudad o municipio, durante su horario normal de oficina, y termina a las 4 p. m. del lunes 2 de noviembre. Llama a la junta de escrutinio local (local board of canvassers) para saber el horario.
early_hours.quote: Early voting will begin on October 14 and end at 4 p.m. on November 2.
early_hours.en_after: Early voting ended at 4 p.m. on November 2. Vote at your polling place on Election Day, 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. (9 a.m. to 8 p.m. in New Shoreham).
early_hours.es_after: La votación anticipada terminó a las 4 p. m. del 2 de noviembre. Vota en tu lugar de votación el Día de las Elecciones, de 7 a. m. a 8 p. m. (de 9 a. m. a 8 p. m. en New Shoreham).

cure.en: Problem with your mail ballot envelope? The attestation form must reach the Board of Elections by 4 p.m. on Tuesday, November 10, 2026.
cure.es: ¿Hay un problema con el sobre de tu boleta por correo? El formulario debe llegar a la Junta de Elecciones a más tardar a las 4 p. m. del martes 10 de noviembre de 2026.
cure.en_after: The deadline for the attestation form was 4 p.m. on Tuesday, November 10, 2026.
cure.es_after: La fecha límite para el formulario fue a las 4 p. m. del martes 10 de noviembre de 2026.
cure.quote: The Deficient Mail Ballot Attestation Form must be received (not just postmarked) by the Board no later than 4:00 p.m. either three (3) days following a primary, or seven (7) days following an election.
cure.notes: Nov 10 computed: seven days after Nov 3, 4 p.m., received not postmarked.

in_person.en: Vote early at the location your city or town designates, or at your polling place on Election Day. Already applied for a mail ballot? If you go to a polling place on Election Day, you'll vote a provisional ballot.
in_person.es: Vota por anticipado en el lugar que designe tu ciudad o municipio, o en tu lugar de votación el Día de las Elecciones. ¿Ya pediste una boleta por correo? Si vas a un lugar de votación el Día de las Elecciones, votarás con una boleta provisional.
in_person.quote: Any person who applied for a mail ballot and attempts to vote at a polling place on Election Day will have to cast a provisional ballot.

rule.en: Find your early voting location, the nearest mail ballot drop box and your Election Day polling place at vote.ri.gov, or ask your local board of canvassers.
rule.es: Busca tu lugar de votación anticipada, el buzón de entrega más cercano y tu lugar de votación del Día de las Elecciones en vote.ri.gov, o pregunta en la junta de escrutinio local (local board of canvassers).
rule.quote: Your early voting location can be found online at vote.ri.gov or by contacting your local board of canvassers.

en: Rhode Island voter identification card, free from the Secretary of State
ID card from a U.S. school, college or university
ID card issued by the United States or the State of Rhode Island
es: Licencia de conducir de Rhode Island
Tarjeta de identificación de votante de Rhode Island, gratis de la Secretaría de Estado
Identificación de una escuela, colegio o universidad de EE. UU.
Tarjeta de identificación militar de EE. UU.
Tarjeta de identificación de Estados Unidos o del estado de Rhode Island
Tarjeta médica emitida por el gobierno
accepted.quote: A valid and current document showing a photograph of the person to whom the document was issued, including without limitation:

expired.en: Your photo ID can be expired, but by no more than six months when you vote.
expired.es: Tu identificación con foto puede estar vencida, pero no más de seis meses al momento de votar.
expired.quote: For purposes of this section, proof of identity shall be valid if unexpired or expired no more than six (6) months prior to voting

without.en: No acceptable photo ID? During early voting, you vote an emergency mail ballot. On Election Day, you vote a provisional ballot, and it counts if your local board finds that the signature on it matches your registration. Need a photo ID? The Department of State issues a free one: call 401-222-2340.
without.es: ¿No tienes una identificación con foto aceptada? Durante la votación anticipada, votas con una boleta de emergencia por correo. El Día de las Elecciones, votas con una boleta provisional, y cuenta si la junta local confirma que tu firma coincide con la de tu registro. ¿Necesitas una identificación con foto? El Departamento de Estado da una gratis: llama al 401-222-2340.
without.quote: If you do not bring an acceptable photo ID when voting in person, you will vote an emergency mail ballot. For a complete list of acceptable photo IDs download this informational flyer. If you do not have a valid photo ID, the Elections Division at the RI Department of State will issue one. Call 401-222-2340 or email elections@sos.ri.gov to learn more.

who.en: Any Rhode Island voter who'd rather not vote in person can vote by mail. Accessible mail ballots are offered too.
who.es: Cualquier votante de Rhode Island que prefiera no votar en persona puede votar por correo. También hay boletas por correo accesibles.
who.quote: Voting by mail is a safe and easy option for those voters who do not want to vote in person.

witness.en: Seal your ballot in the certificate envelope, then sign and date it. Put that envelope in the return envelope. Can't sign your name? An assistant fills out the Voter Assistant Certification.
witness.es: Mete tu boleta en el sobre de certificado (Voter's Mail Ballot Certificate Envelope), ciérralo, fírmalo y ponle la fecha. Mete ese sobre en el sobre de devolución. ¿No puedes firmar? Una persona que te ayude llena la certificación de asistente (Voter Assistant Certification).
witness.quote: If you are unable to sign your name, an assistant must complete the Voter Assistant Certification. Place the Voter’s Mail Ballot Certificate Envelope into the Return Envelope.

cure.en: If there's a problem with your mail ballot envelope, you'll be notified by phone, text or mail. The Deficient Mail Ballot Attestation Form must reach the Board of Elections, not just be postmarked, by 4 p.m. on Tuesday, November 10.
cure.es: Si hay un problema con el sobre de tu boleta por correo, te avisarán por teléfono, mensaje de texto o correo. El formulario Deficient Mail Ballot Attestation debe llegar a la Junta de Elecciones, no solo tener matasellos, a más tardar a las 4 p. m. del martes 10 de noviembre.
cure.quote: The Deficient Mail Ballot Attestation Form must be received (not just postmarked) by the Board no later than 4:00 p.m. either three (3) days following a primary, or seven (7) days following an election.
cure.notes: Nov 10 computed: seven days after Nov 3, 4 p.m., received not postmarked.
cure.en_after: The deadline for the attestation form was 4 p.m. on Tuesday, November 10, 2026.
cure.es_after: La fecha límite para el formulario fue a las 4 p. m. del martes 10 de noviembre de 2026.

dropbox.en: Drop it in a 24-hour elections drop box by 8 p.m. on Election Day. On Election Day, every polling place also has a drop box for mail ballots.
dropbox.es: Déjala en un buzón electoral abierto las 24 horas a más tardar a las 8 p. m. del Día de las Elecciones. Ese día, cada lugar de votación también tiene un buzón para boletas por correo.
dropbox.quote: NOTE: All polling places will also have drop boxes for your voted mail ballot.

gear.en: You can wear a campaign button, pin or shirt, but vote and then leave. No one can hand out or post campaign material inside the polling place or within 50 feet of the voter entrance.
gear.es: Puedes llevar un botón, un pin o una camiseta de campaña, pero vota y luego retírate. Nadie puede repartir ni colocar material de campaña dentro del lugar de votación ni a menos de 50 pies de la entrada de votantes.
gear.quote: 1. Voters may wear political campaign materials like buttons, pins, shirts, etc. However, they are expected to vote and leave the polling place. ... 6. No campaign material should be distributed or posted within 50 feet of the voter entrance to the building.

phone.en: You can take a photo of your own ballot, and general photos are fine outside the voting area. Texting is allowed if it doesn't get in the way of voting. Phone calls inside the polling place aren't allowed unless they're about the election. That's from the Board of Elections' July 2024 poll worker manual.
phone.es: Puedes tomarle una foto a tu propia boleta, y las fotos en general están permitidas fuera del área de votación. Puedes mandar mensajes de texto si no interfieres con la votación. No se permiten llamadas dentro del lugar de votación, salvo que sean sobre la elección. Así lo dice el manual para trabajadores electorales de la Junta Electoral (Board of Elections), de julio de 2024.
phone.quote: 3. Photographs of a voter’s own ballot are allowed. General photography is also allowed outside the voter area. Inform any news media that they may not zoom in on a voter’s ballot, which would violate the voter’s privacy.

line.en: In line at 8 p.m.? Stay in line. Anyone waiting in line to vote at 8 p.m. gets to vote.
line.es: ¿Estás en la fila a las 8 p. m.? Quédate en la fila. Cualquier persona que esté esperando en la fila para votar a las 8 p. m. puede votar.
line.quote: provided, that any qualified voter who is waiting in line to vote at 8 p.m. shall be entitled to cast his or her vote.

tradition.en: In Cranston, high school students design the city's I Voted stickers. The Board of Canvassers started the contest in 2025, reviewed 10 finalists picked by the School Department, and chose four 2026 designs, by Samantha, Lexi, Grace and Julia, for Cranston polling places.
tradition.es: En Cranston, estudiantes de preparatoria diseñan los stickers de "I Voted" de la ciudad. La junta de escrutinio (Board of Canvassers) creó el concurso en 2025, revisó 10 finalistas elegidos por el Departamento Escolar y escogió cuatro diseños de 2026, de Samantha, Lexi, Grace y Julia, para los lugares de votación de Cranston.
tradition.quote: The Board of Canvassers publicly reviewed 10 finalists from students, which were selected by the School Department, and selected designs to print in accordance with the contest policies. ... congratulations to those whose artwork was selected for use at Cranston polling places!

early.en: Yes. The Department of State's early voting steps end with returning the empty secrecy folder and wearing your "I voted" sticker.
early.es: Sí. Los pasos de la votación anticipada del Departamento de Estado terminan con devolver la carpeta de privacidad vacía y ponerte tu sticker de "I voted".

mail.en: Yes. Rhode Island puts an "I Voted by Mail" sticker in every mail ballot packet, along with your ballot, the certificate envelope, the instructions and a postage-paid return envelope.
mail.es: Sí. Rhode Island incluye un sticker de “I Voted by Mail” en cada paquete de boleta por correo, junto con tu boleta, el sobre del certificado, las instrucciones y un sobre de devolución con franqueo pagado.
mail.quote: Your mail ballot packet includes: Your mail ballot Voter's Mail Ballot Certificate envelope Vote by Mail instructions wrap Postage-paid return envelope I Voted by Mail sticker
mail.notes: Department of State Vote by Mail page, read in Chrome Oct 30 (curl gets 403); first seen in pass 2.

provisional.en: On Election Day, you vote a provisional ballot if your name isn't on the voter list, you don't have an acceptable photo ID, you applied for a mail ballot, or there's another question about your eligibility. Your local board of canvassers decides after Election Day whether it counts. Check the result at elections.ri.gov or by calling 401-222-2345.
provisional.es: El Día de las Elecciones, votas con una boleta provisional si tu nombre no está en la lista de votantes, no tienes una identificación con foto aceptada, pediste una boleta por correo o hay otra duda sobre si puedes votar. La junta de escrutinio local (local board of canvassers) decide después del Día de las Elecciones si cuenta. Revisa el resultado en elections.ri.gov o llamando al 401-222-2345.
provisional.quote: The voter may learn the disposition of the ballot by visiting elections.ri.gov or by calling the State Board of Elections at 401-222-2345.

line.en: You can still vote. Anyone waiting in line to vote at 8 p.m. gets to vote.
line.es: Todavía puedes votar. Cualquier persona que esté esperando en la fila para votar a las 8 p. m. puede votar.
line.quote: provided, that any qualified voter who is waiting in line to vote at 8 p.m. shall be entitled to cast his or her vote.

track.en: Sign up at vote.ri.gov to track your mail ballot. You'll get updates when it's mailed to you and when the Board of Elections receives it.
track.es: Inscríbete en vote.ri.gov para seguir tu boleta por correo. Recibirás avisos cuando te la envíen y cuando la reciba la Junta Electoral (Board of Elections).
track.quote: You will receive updates when your ballot is placed in the mail and when it is received by the Board of Elections for certification.

late_mail.en: It may be. The Board of Elections must receive it by 8 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3, and the state says to allow seven mailing days. Instead, put it in any official elections drop box, or on Election Day in the ballot box at any polling place. You can also hand it in at the Board of Elections in Cranston.
late_mail.es: Puede que sí. La Junta de Elecciones (Board of Elections) debe recibirla a más tardar a las 8 p. m. del martes 3 de noviembre, y el estado recomienda dejar siete días para el correo. Mejor déjala en cualquier buzón oficial de entrega o, el Día de las Elecciones, en el receptáculo para boletas de cualquier lugar de votación. También puedes entregarla en la Junta de Elecciones en Cranston.
late_mail.quote: Allow at least seven (7) mailing days to ensure your mail ballot arrives by 8 p.m. on Election Day. Option 2: Hand deliver the sealed envelope to any official elections drop box located around the state. Use the Drop Box locator or contact your local board of canvassers to find a drop box near you. On Election Day, all polling places also have a receptacle in which you can deposit your sealed ballot. Option 3: Hand deliver the sealed envelope to the Board of Elections: 2000 Plainfield Pike, Suite A Cranston, RI 02921 The Board of Elections must receive your mail ballot by 8 p.m. on Election Day
late_mail.notes: Pass 2 Oct 30, read in Chrome (blocks curl). Same page: the mail ballot packet includes an 'I Voted by Mail sticker' (sticker lead for the RI page).

notes: Read October 21, 2026. vote.sos.ri.gov and elections.ri.gov HTML pages return 403 to curl; the 2026 Rhode Island Voter Information Handbook PDF (vote.sos.ri.gov/Forms/Elections/Guides/VoterRef26.pdf, read with pdftotext) and RI General Laws on webserver.rilegislature.gov (17-9.1-3, 17-18-11, 17-19-24.2, 17-19-24.3, 17-19-49) were used. vote.ri.gov 301-redirects to vote.sos.ri.gov. Early voting dates match states.js (October 14 to November 2); the handbook adds that early voting ends at 4 p.m. on November 2 ('Early voting will begin on October 14 and end at 4 p.m. on November 2.') and elsewhere says 'during their regular business hours'. Registration: October 4, 2026 is a Sunday and 17-9.1-3 says local boards don't take registrations on Sundays; the file states the 30-day rule and date, as the FAQ does. The October 27 mail-by date is the handbook's 'at least seven days before Election Day', not a separate official date. Mail ballot cure, phone rules, first-time voter rules and a sticker contest on an official page were not found; left missing. The Board of Elections' sticker contest (reported by ABC6) is on elections.ri.gov, which returns 403. No county or town office list URL was confirmed online (the handbook lists local boards of canvassers on page 17). Oct 28 pass: early-voting no-ID rule from vote.sos.ri.gov/Voter/PersonVotingPage (Chrome); emergency mail ballot deadline from 17-20-2.2(b) (4 p.m. the day before the election), and the VoteByMail page FAQ ('If you cannot vote in-person, you may request an emergency mail ballot from your local board of canvassers'); hand delivery to 2000 Plainfield Pike from the VoteByMail page. Phones, photos and campaign clothing from the Board of Elections poll worker manual (July 2024, the latest posted; read with pdftotext). Cranston sticker story from cranstonri.gov (Civics and Elections); the page names the four students in full, and only first names are kept here because they are high school students. The handbook says mailed applications postmarked by October 13 count if received within three days (17-20-2.1(c)); not added because it is past. ID list matches 17-19-24.2; Perplexity's 'permit' and 'tribal ID' are not in the statute and were not added. The Nov 10 cure deadline stays on the 410-RICR-20-00-23 reading of Oct 26. VoteByMail FAQ: 'Rhode Island allows same-day voter registration for presidential elections only.'

hours.en: Polling places are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.; New Shoreham opens at 9 a.m.
hours.es: Los lugares de votación abren de 7 a. m. a 8 p. m.; New Shoreham abre a las 9 a. m.
hours.quote: All polling places in the state open at 7:00 a.m. and close at 8 p.m., with the exception of New Shoreham, which opens at 9 a.m.
